supporting_observations.claim: The periodic HTTPS activity is consistently attributable to C:\Program Files\LedgerLink\ledgerlinkupd.exe (ProcessId 4804), which connects through the proxy to update.ledgerlink.com.

The observed connections recur at approximately five-minute intervals, and the inventory identifies LedgerLink as checking update.ledgerlink.com about every five minutes. This strongly matches the alerted behavior.

The updater process was started by Chrome, whose recorded command line references https://graph.microsoft.com/; this is an unusual launch relationship, but the available records do not establish that it is malicious.

known_telemetry_limitations: The proxy records show HTTPS CONNECT tunnels and metadata, not the updater's encrypted request or response contents.
The records provide the updater's image path but no file hash or signature-validation result.
claims_not_established: Whether the LedgerLink executable is authentic and unmodified.
Why Chrome launched the updater, or whether that parent-child relationship was expected.
Whether the updater retrieved or applied any update during these connections.
unrelated_findings: Google Drive File Stream started on WS-MFISCHER-01, and the user later accessed drive.google.com; Google Drive is an unapproved cloud-storage service in the provided inventory. Track separately; this does not determine the LedgerLink alert disposition. (T226-00134, T226-00135, T226-00136, T226-00395, T226-00396, T226-00400, T226-00402)
